findings.claim: Hiding a positive leaves its bookkeeping in the diff stat the judge reads, and the filter's signals see it too. hide.visible_files drops only .okf/decisions/ paths. Over the draft's 161 units, .okf/log.md is touched by 31 of 31 positives and 31 of 130 negatives, and .okf/summary.md by 13 of 31 against 26 of 130. The text keeps tells as well: 0013's intent still says 'The number follows release-flow's 0012; the builder takes the next free one', and 0030's says '.okf/summary.md cites it' and 'No code changes'. On a real gap no decision was written, so the log, summary and index lines tied to it would not be there. As written, recall for both the filter and the judge is inflated by an artefact of the hiding. The plan should hide the decision's log, index and summary lines too, or drop .okf/ bookkeeping paths from every unit's view, positives and negatives alike, and say which.

spike:decision-gaps-measure/1 does not settle the risk it is cited for. leak_check.py strips text with hide.strip, which drops every sentence matching hide.LEAK, then tests the result with hide.leaks, which is the same LEAK regex. leaky_after_strip=0 is therefore true by construction for any input and measures nothing. The spike's own outcome says it is 'settled for the words, not for the shape', and the shape (p1) is exactly what is left open. A second spike is needed. Question: with the decision files and their log, index and summary lines hidden, can a check that does not share strip's regex tell hidden positives from negatives better than chance? Two candidates: a list of .okf/ paths only, or a separate word list (chose, choice, rejected, record, four-digit numbers in the ADR range, 'next free one').

Some positives are units that record a decision made somewhere else, so once the decision is hidden nothing decision-shaped is left. Examples: 0030 (commit-apm-installs, 0 files outside .okf/ and .loop/, 'No code changes', the choice made when PR #16 was closed), and the small PR units for 0033 and 0034 (6 and 13 files). Counting them as misses pulls recall down. Counting the earlier unit that made the choice as a negative pushes the false-alarm rate up, unless that unit's claim is labelled correct. The plan should say how record-only positives are counted: kept out of the recall denominator or reported apart, and their originating unit labelled as a real gap. Otherwise the recall figure means something other than 'finds a decision made in this unit'.

The plan does not say how many negatives the judge reads, or what recall, precision and cost would justify building. With 31 positive units, one miss moves recall by about 3 points, and a 95% interval near 80% spans roughly 63 to 92%. A negative sample of a dozen would leave precision just as loose. Without a stated sample size and bar, the README's build or don't-build verdict is read after the numbers are seen, so the decision G1 asks for is not one the measurement can settle. Name the negative sample size, chosen for an acceptable interval on the false-alarm rate, and the thresholds that would mean build, build with changes, or don't build.

Bookkeeping paths and words leaked positives. hide.visible_files now drops every .okf/ and .loop/ path for every unit alike, and LEAK also drops sentences naming .okf/, summary.md, log.md, 'next free' and 'the number'. signals.py and judge.py both read only visible_files and strip output.

Spike 1 could not fail. Spike 2 checks with detectors that share nothing with strip: visible bookkeeping paths score AUC 0.50 and a separate record-keeping word list AUC 0.64, and the plan names that residue for the README.

Record-only positives now have a rule: a positive whose unit changes nothing outside .okf/ and .loop/ is reported apart, out of the recall count (only ADR 0030 in the range), and row r2 fails if one is counted in recall.

The judge runs on all 161 units, not a sample, and the bars are set before the run: recall >= 70% with Wilson lower end >= 50%, precision of claims on negatives >= 50%, range cost <= $10. Row r2 checks the README's verdict against them.

The README description, the prototypes index entry and the log entry say "9 of its 17 claims elsewhere were real gaps", but the judge made 32 claims on negatives; 17 is only the gap plus false-alarm subset after 15 recorded-in-unit claims were set aside.

The README does not say how much the precision bar depends on labelling choices. It sets aside the 15 recorded-in-unit claims, a category the plan never defined (the plan says a correct claim counts as a hit, which would give 24/32, 75%). It counts the MIT licence twice (ce8b712c and its PR
leak_check.py's usage line names scripts/leak_spike.py, which is not in the folder.

signals.py's docstring says decision records and the decision index are dropped, and judge.py's says decision records are hidden. hide.visible_files actually drops every path under .okf/ and .loop/ for every unit.
The README says the 0.64 word residue comes "mostly" from "summary" and "bundle", but no script in the folder prints a per-word breakdown, so that claim cannot be rerun.

Row r3's command runs test_docs_frontmatter.py. That covers kmctl check over the repository (test_this_repo_docs_are_migrated), but not the strict OKF validation the row names. I ran the validator by hand and it reports the bundle conformant.
